lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: the structure of a deductive proof
lessonRef.title: Independent application A: the structure of a deductive proof

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One reference example. Use it only if you get stuck.

items.prompt: Remote interior angles 40° and 65°. Exterior angle?

steps: Exterior equals the sum of the remote interiors.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: In a parallelogram, one angle measures 108°. Find the consecutive angle.
In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 44. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
choices: 88, and it is parallel to the third side
22, and it is perpendicular to the third side
44, and it is parallel to the third side
22, and it is parallel to the third side

items.prompt: A proof concludes that base angles of an isosceles triangle are congruent, after constructing the bisector of the apex angle. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
choices: All triangles have congruent base angles.
The two smaller triangles are congruent by SAS, so their corresponding base angles are congruent.
The bisector is perpendicular to the base by definition.
The base angles look equal in the diagram.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 33°. Find the measure of the co-interior (same-side interior) angle.
In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 23° and 57°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.
In a parallelogram, one angle measures 86°. Find the consecutive angle.
In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 26. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
choices: 26, and it is parallel to the third side
13, and it is parallel to the third side
52, and it is parallel to the third side
13, and it is perpendicular to the third side

items.prompt: A proof concludes that vertical angles are congruent. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
choices: The two lines are parallel, forcing the angles to match.
Each vertical angle is supplementary to the same adjacent angle, so both have the same measure.
The angles are congruent because they are opposite in position.
Vertical angles are congruent by definition.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 78°. Find the measure of the alternate interior angle.
In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 42° and 62°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.
In a parallelogram, one angle measures 102°. Find the opposite angle.
